Designed as a control plane

One safety story.
Every surface accounted for.

Repayd’s job is not to replace your stack. It makes autonomous payments legible across it.

◈ Arc

Settlement

Policy and recovery contracts on the Arc testnet, with explorer-ready receipts.

Arc explorer ↗
  • Six contracts on Arc testnet
  • Caps: 200/tx · 1,000/day · 5 tx
  • 30-tx run, 6/6 checks passed
  • $135 same-block payout
The Graph

Memory

Protocol state and ERC-8004 mirrors become one queryable, composable record.

See the record ↗
  • repayd-risk-arc v0.1.3
  • repayd (ERC-8004) v0.1.1
  • Joined by agentId
  • Agent 894341: score 25, −2500@2dp
◆ Hedera

Metering

x402 access and HCS audit trails show the surface beyond a single chain.

Follow the story ↗
  • x402 via Blocky402 facilitator
  • 0.001 ℏ settled per request
  • HCS topic 0.0.10493275
  • Schedule 0.0.10493353
◎ ENS

Identity

A public résumé layer for agents with a history worth discovering.

Explore identity ↗
  • atlasrepayd.eth on Sepolia
  • ENSv2 permissioned resolver
  • Full résumé in text records
  • Resolved, not fixture data

No hidden footnotes

Good safety UX makes the limits obvious.

Start with the story. Inspect the assumptions when you want the depth. The product should never make you decode its architecture before you can use it.

Is this a live product? +

It is a testnet prototype with real Arc transactions and mintable Demo USDC. It demonstrates the protocol behavior; it is not real-money insurance.

What does the watcher actually prove? +

The watcher and attack facts in the demo are explicitly local, scripted inputs. Chain receipts remain chain receipts. Repayd does not label a local signer as a live TEE.

What should I do first? +

Open the live demo, press Run demo, and follow the event journal. Then open the Agent record to see the evidence and standard-registry mirror.

A safer default for agent economies

Explore the live testnet story. No wallet connection required. No black boxes required.
